conventions.source: staging/blender/2026-11-22_round4/round4.blend (saved from reactions5.blend), scene RD, one station per look (x from 120000, 40 m apart, order in tools/rd_order.json). Built by script (tools/b1.py to b4.py on tools/rdcommon.py) from the reactions-4 and reactions-5 specs where a look keeps what the owner liked, the elements 2, 3 and 4 kits, combo kits v3, r4 and r5, and the new kit vfx_round4_kit.fbx.
conventions.made: 2026-11-22 by Claude through the Blender MCP connection.
conventions.axes: Unity axes, metres. Unity x = -Blender x, Unity y = Blender z (up), Unity z = -Blender y. Assumes the kit FBX files are imported with Bake Axis Conversion so each kit object's local axes are Unity axes.
conventions.origin: Every position is relative to the main body's ground point (y = 0): the body point 3 m out from the player along the line player to body. Pieces with on_player (and ribbons whose centre is player) are relative to the player's ground point. Offsets are world-aligned to the camera (it looks along Unity +z from -z, 55 degrees down).
conventions.groups: Pieces that share kit object and material are grouped. Each instance is [object, position, rotation_euler_deg, scale, placement], the KEY POSE (before any motion channel). group.motion lists the same objects in the same order.
conventions.instance.rotation_euler_deg: Unity Euler angles in degrees (Quaternion.Euler(x, y, z)), rounded to 1 degree.
conventions.instance.position: Metres, rounded to 1 mm: the piece's pivot (its base centre, the kit convention; the sword, dagger, funnel and whirl bands, rays and soft rays pivot at their origin: the guard, or the axis foot).
conventions.instance.scale: A number for uniform scale, else [x, y, z] in Unity local axes.
conventions.instance.placement: g = on the ground, b = on or around a body (or in the bowl), p = on the player.
conventions.group.kit_object: The object inside group.kit. A kit of enemy_model means a second skin of the enemy model itself (stone, black) shown over it in the given window; unity_shader_mockup means a shell to build as a shader on the real model.
conventions.group.material: The material the piece wears in the render (shared meshes are re-coloured per piece). Flat emission bands, as pass 2.
conventions.timing: animated. Every piece is keyed at 20 fps; time 0 is frame 7 (frames 1-6 are a 0.3 s lead-in), and each timeline ends with 0.5 s of settle.
conventions.motion: One entry per instance (same order): verb, visible [appear, vanish] s (a vanish of 9 or more means it stays), delay = appear time, duration, easing, and the channels: path = [[t, offset (Unity axes, world-aligned), easing into this key]], scale_keys = [[t, multiplier on the key-pose scale (Unity local x, y, z), easing]], spin = {axis (Unity), keys [[t, degrees, easing]]} applied as Quaternion.AngleAxis(degrees, axis) * keyRotation about the pivot, orbit = {centre (Unity, from the origin), keys [[t, degrees, easing]]} applied last about the vertical through the centre, follow_body = the body index whose motion the piece rides on. Before the first key a channel holds its first value, after the last its last. Easings: linear, out = 1-(1-x)^2, in = x^2, inout = smoothstep, outback = overshoot (c = 1.70158), step = jump at the key. Angles are in Unity's sense.
conventions.bodies: The enemy model (enemy_husk stand-in) per body with its own motion (path, scale_keys, spin, spin2 applied after spin); body 0 is the one the reaction lands on. The stand-ins face the player.
conventions.lights: None: every look is unlit beyond the scene sun.
conventions.ribbons: Curve ribbons (wind curls, lightning arcs, floor combs, chains of light) are not kit meshes: each lists its points (Unity axes, metres, relative to its centre), width_m, radius_profile (taper = thin tail to full head scaled by taper_tail_head; needle = thin at both ends; flat = even), material and ink. Build them as a tube or flat ribbon along the points with the ink outline.

verbs.ribbon_draw: draw_on = [[t, fraction, easing]]: how much is drawn from tail to head (the head leads). erase = [[t, fraction, easing]]: how much is wiped from the tail toward the head. Visible length = draw_on - erase; nothing pops in or out.
verbs.orbit: centre (player, station or body n), radius (m), turns_per_second (Unity sense, + = counter-clockwise from above), start (s), rise (m per s), and optional angle_keys added on top. The ribbon turns about the vertical axis through its centre from start.
verbs.spiral: an orbit with rise > 0: the ribbon climbs while it turns.

conventions.blade_frame: The charged-blade looks swing a stand-in katana (vfxe3_katana) about the player: it and its sheaths (vfxe3_flameflag_a/b, iceteeth, watersheath, thornvine, stonespine, edgelight, venomcoat) share one frame with the pivot at the hilt end: the blade along local +x (Blender; Unity -x after the axis bake), grip 0 to 0.27 m, guard 0.27 to 0.30 m, blade 0.30 to 1.25 m, the edge facing local +y (Blender), the flat facing up. Their motion.orbit (centre_is player) is the swing: three cuts 0.45 s apart. In Unity, parent the sheath to the real weapon's blade bone with the same frame scaled to the blade length; the orbit keys are the mock-up of the weapon animation, not data to play.
conventions.scale: Stand-in enemies are 1.89 m tall, the size of the castle soldiers. Pieces were drawn to read at the game camera (12.7 m); keep their size relative to the body in game, not to the screen.
conventions.colour: Materials are flat emission in linear colour (the toon stone and stand-in bodies excepted); no stop reaches pure white. The strip maker counts pure-white pixels per frame (white_check.json): every look is 0.
conventions.look_fields: Each look carries element, moment, owner (the fourth-review comment, quoted, and the plan's direction), answer (how the look answers it), look (in words), revision_of where it replaces an earlier look, strip (the beats) and round.
conventions.timing_round4: Every round-4 look is 1.5 s (cause, impact, aftermath), on the 20 fps timeline with t 0 at frame 7; pieces with a visible end of 9 stay to the end of the effect.
conventions.motion.body: The body (index into bodies; 0 is the main body) the piece belongs to: it is placed about that body and shown on it. Restored from the pass's own specs (staging/blender/2026-11-22_round4/tools/specs_*.gltf) by AgentScripts/recipe_bodies.py, as the export wrote only follow_body and orbit.centre_is. Numbers in a piece's name are not bodies (spark15, heavechip4). Pieces on the player carry on_player instead.

owner: 2026-11-21 (fourth review), Rime: "The rime crystals blowing into enemies and chilling them visual is terrible, the concept is good, but the visuals for that part need to be scrapped and reworked"

The owner on the round-4 strip (2026-11-22): "I dont like the lines in the ground for rime, i would rather the cold gusts carrying the frost over". No frost lines on the ground; cold gusts as Wind-style curls in pale icy blue, never mint, carry the frost over; rime feathers grow where they reach.
looks.answer: Round 2. The build-up is kept (cold curls wrap it, now pale icy blue, and rime builds on its back), 25% quicker. Nothing lies on the ground. At the heavy, cold gusts tear the rime off its back: two fat Wind-style gusts per enemy, pale icy blue with a brighter upper edge, sweep in curving arcs from its back over to each of the three others, crystals of rime riding inside them, and wind round each one in an open curl. Where they strike, rime feathers grow on the side the cold came from, pointing into the wind, from the feet up.
looks.look: Cold wind wraps the enemy and rime builds on its back. The heavy sets cold gusts loose: they tear the rime off its back and carry it in curving pale-blue gusts over to the others, winding round each one, and rime feathers grow on them where the gusts strike.

owner: 2026-11-21 (fourth review), Quickening: "The intial seeds effect when its jumpy is not good, and the plants that spring up dont have flowers and are not blue. The stem should be green, but the flower on top should be blue. Also if you are getting healed you should give off a green pulse, instead of green crystals flowing to you"
looks.answer: No seeds: the circling seeds and the seeds flung at the near ones are gone, so nothing jumps. The plants are new: seven green stems spring up round its feet where the water ran down, each with two green leaves and a BLUE flower opening on top (six cupped blue petals, a gold heart); the blue flower on its chest is gone, so the heavy now bursts the water held in it straight out in a splash. The heal is a green pulse on you: soft green light runs up your body from the feet to the head twice, like a heartbeat, and lifts off as motes. Nothing flies to you.
looks.look: One big drop falls on the enemy and splashes; green stems spring up round its feet and blue flowers open on top of them. The heavy bursts the water out of it in a splash that soaks the near ones, and a green pulse of light runs up your body twice as you are healed.

owner: 2026-11-21 (fourth review), Diamond Ring: "Move the portal a little off the enemy, and have the light chains going into the portal, and not have the after effect of cursed afflictions"

The owner on the round-4 strip (2026-11-22), through the coordinator: the portal is a ragged tear of darkness with a soft gold edge, with no clean ring outline; the chains are solid links that read at the game camera, not a dotted line.
looks.answer: Round 2. The portal is now a ragged tear of darkness: an upright rip with a jagged, uneven edge (near-black violet), ringed by no clean outline at all, only a soft gold edge in two steps (a gold rim and a deeper amber glow behind it, both as ragged as the tear) with gold flecks flickering off it. It rips open beside the enemy, about 1.5 m off its body to its left as you look. Each of the three critical blows shoots a solid chain of gold light (new mesh rdk_chain: fat interlocked links, inked) from the Marked star on its chest into the tear, which draws it in link by link with a gold flash; the third drags the star in. Then the tear seals. Nothing is left on the enemy or the floor.
looks.look: A ragged tear of darkness with a soft gold edge rips open beside the marked enemy. Each critical blow shoots a solid chain of gold light from the star on its chest into the tear, which draws it in; the last chain drags the star in and the tear seals. Nothing is left behind.

The owner on the round-4 strip (2026-11-22), through the coordinator: no circle on the floor; the jar's ribs only. The cloud inside is a dark, rolling, sickly green with volume, not a flat lime blob.
looks.answer: Round 2. Nothing on the floor: the black sealing ring and the hole are gone, so the jar is its smooth black ribs with violet edges alone, arching in over its head, and their shards when it breaks. Inside it the one cloud is now dark and sickly green (rd_sickcloud, from near-black green to a sickly olive) and has volume: seven lobes stacked from the floor to its shoulders, rolling over one another and turning, pressing on the ribs. When the jar breaks the cloud bursts outward, a rolling puff of it flies to each near enemy, and each (and the first) is simply Poisoned: the affliction's own small puffs pop off it.
looks.look: Smooth black ribs close over the cursed, poisoned enemy into a jar, and one dark, sickly green cloud fills it, its lobes rolling over one another. The jar breaks, the cloud bursts out to the near enemies, and they are Poisoned: small puffs pop off them. Nothing is left on the floor.

owner: 2026-11-21 (fourth review), Carried Embers: "The fire winds flying out are way too crazy this needs to be reworked"
The plan (2026-11-22): one small, tight whirl of embers and flame curls down its lane, lighting only what it touches.
looks.answer: The big bending fire whirl, its wide bands and the shreds of flame flung off it are gone. Now one small, tight whirl (1.6 m tall, 0.85 m across at the top) of thin flame curls and sixteen whirling embers sets off from the burning enemy and walks 4.3 m down the lane in 0.8 s. Only what it touches catches: as it passes over each of the two enemies on the lane, sparks burst on it, it flinches and small flames catch on it; the enemy 2.4 m off the lane is never touched. At the end of its run the whirl just loosens, rises and is gone; its embers drift up and go out.
looks.look: Wind wraps the burning enemy and its flame is drawn into one small, tight whirl of embers and flame that walks down the lane. Each enemy it touches flinches and catches fire; the one off the lane does not. At the end of its run the whirl loosens and is gone.

owner: 2026-11-21 (fourth review), Winter Seed: "The first effect looks like water and life, until the ice flower blooms, the water dropping does not look like ice"
The owner on the round-4 strip (2026-11-22), through the coordinator: bigger sleet pellets that bounce and frost the ground where they land.
looks.answer: Round 2. The water drips are gone. The frost on the sleeping enemy cracks from the top down and sheds big sleet pellets (rdk_pellet at 0.27 m, pale, faceted, inked): they fall, bounce once and lie, and where each strikes the ground, frost spreads in a small star of rime (at the strike and where it comes to rest). Beads of frost glint on the crust as it cracks. The lotus, the stamens, the hooked ice thorns and the frost are kept; the seeds are the warm golden-brown of the new Seeded, and the heal is the stronger green pulse on you.
looks.look: The seeded enemy sleeps under frost. The frost cracks from the top down and sheds big sleet pellets that bounce and frost the ground where they land. It falls, and where it lay an ice lotus opens and hooked ice thorns burst up; a green pulse runs up you.
